# Results — Study 392 (Glassdoor-Sentiment)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The folk claim — **"companies
with the happiest employees beat the market"** (the retail descendant of Edmans 2011's
"100 Best Companies to Work For" premium) — tested by sorting a fixed large-cap basket on a
**constructed, clearly-labelled employee-satisfaction proxy** and trading the happiest-minus-
grumpiest long-short. Real Glassdoor / employer-review data is **not free**, so the sentiment
score here is an EXPLICIT placeholder (NOT scraped ratings), assigned independently of
returns — the honest null. The synthetic control plants a known happiness→return edge to
prove the engine is faithful. Offline & deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — fixed 40-name US large-cap basket (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-18 (**5,399** trading days; **21.5** years; **257** monthly spreads) |
| Sentiment input | **CONSTRUCTED proxy** — a fixed-seed 1.0–5.0 "stars" score per name, **independent of returns** (NOT real Glassdoor data) |
| Sort | happiest quintile (Q5) long − grumpiest quintile (Q1) short, equal-weight, static score |
| Entry / costs | 1-period (monthly) execution lag; 10 bps one-way × turnover (2 legs) + 50 bps/yr short borrow |

> **Proxy caveat (named on the Signal axis).** This study cannot buy the real ratings, so it
> sorts on a *constructed* satisfaction score that, by construction, carries **no** information
> about returns. The real-tape result is therefore an honest **null**, and a proxy/synthetic-
> only result can **never** back a `REAL` stamp. The contribution is the *method* (a faithful,
> leak-free happiness long-short with a placebo null) plus the literature map — not a validated
> live edge. Drop a genuine Glassdoor feed into `data.constructed_sentiment`'s replacement
> argument and the same engine re-runs on the real thing.

## The signal — happiest-minus-grumpiest long-short on the constructed proxy

One-period entry lag; the spread is equal-weight Q5 − Q1 each month. The one-sample *t* tests
the mean monthly spread against zero (the no-premium null); the placebo *p* is the share of
random **relabellings** of which names are "happy" vs "grumpy" whose mean spread matches or
beats the real one in magnitude.

| metric | value |
|---|--:|
| months | 257 |
| mean monthly spread | **+0.27%** |
| annualised spread | **+3.3%** |
| one-sample *t* (vs 0) | **+1.16** |
| annualised Sharpe | **0.25** |
| Sharpe 95% bootstrap CI | **[−0.16, +0.67]** |
| win-rate (months > 0) | **54%** |
| placebo *p* (relabelling null) | **0.16** |

Read it carefully. The long-short is mildly *positive* (+3.3%/yr) — but at **t = 1.16** it
**fails the t ≥ 2 bar**, the **Sharpe CI straddles zero** (−0.16 to +0.67), the monthly
win-rate (**54%**) is a coin-flip, and a random relabelling of the happiness scores matches it
**~1 time in 6** (placebo p = 0.16). On a sentiment input that is *by construction* unrelated
to returns, this is exactly the null we should see — there is nothing here the chance of a
40-name sort can't produce.

## Costs — they barely move it (frequency/turnover is not the issue here)

| metric | gross | net @ 10 bps × turnover + 50 bps borrow |
|---|--:|--:|
| mean monthly spread | +0.273% | +0.215% |
| annualised Sharpe | 0.25 | 0.20 |

A static-score factor rebalances rarely, so the **70 bps/yr** all-in cost shaves the Sharpe
from 0.25 to 0.20 — it does **not** rescue or destroy the result. The binding fact is upstream:
the gross spread is already statistically indistinguishable from zero.

## Robustness — flat in the quintile fraction, flat across constructed panels

| quintile fraction *q* | ann. spread | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.10 (top/bottom 4 names) | +2.4% | 0.71 | 0.438 |
| **0.20** (top/bottom 8 names) | +3.3% | **1.16** | 0.160 |
| 0.30 (top/bottom 12 names) | +2.3% | 0.99 | 0.236 |

There is no cut at which the *t* approaches 2. And across **10 independent constructed
satisfaction panels** (seeds 392–401) the largest |*t*| observed is **1.57** — no panel clears
the significance bar. The null is robust, not a single unlucky draw.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, and recovers a *planted* edge

A fully synthetic monthly panel (240 months, 40 names) where each name's satisfaction score is
known and monthly returns carry a **planted** cross-sectional happiness tilt of magnitude
`edge`:

| planted edge (per-σ-star, monthly) | ann. spread | one-sample *t* | Sharpe | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.000** (no edge) | +1.7% | **0.83** | 0.19 | 0.448 |
| **+0.010** (large edge) | +15.8% | **7.91** | 1.77 | 0.000 |

With **no** planted edge the long-short stays at **t = 0.83** (below 2 — the engine does **not**
manufacture significance from noise). With a large planted edge it lights up at **t = 7.91 /
p = 0.000**. The control proves two things at once: the measurement engine is **unbiased**, and
the real-tape null is an *honest* null — the detector finds an edge when one is truly there, and
correctly finds nothing on a sentiment proxy that is unrelated to returns.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The academic premium (Edmans 2011) is real *in the literature*, but this
  study can only test the claim on a **constructed proxy** with no built-in link to returns, on
  which the happiness long-short is **+3.3%/yr at t = 1.16** (placebo p = 0.16, Sharpe CI
  crosses zero) — it **fails the t ≥ 2 bar**. Proxy/synthetic-only support ⇒ **WEAK**, never
  `REAL`. The Signal axis also carries **survivorship** (a fixed surviving-large-cap basket) and
  the **proxy** caveat explicitly.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** A static-score quintile long-short trades rarely, so the **70 bps/yr**
  all-in cost only trims the Sharpe from 0.25 to 0.20 — but a long-short whose gross Sharpe is
  **0.25 with a CI through zero** is not a NAV-scale, deployable strategy. Even granting the
  literature its real premium, *this* implementation, on *this* proxy, has no edge to deploy.
- **Free lunch? — BUSTED.** "Buy the happiest workplaces and beat the market" is, on a
  return-independent sentiment proxy, indistinguishable from a coin-flip (54% monthly win-rate,
  placebo p = 0.16). The romance of the alt-data narrative does the work the data cannot.
